findingDetails.title: Current-generation fingerprints omit acceptance criteria from the hashed source set
findingDetails.evidence: CANONICAL_PACKET_DOCS omits acceptance-criteria.md while generated-metadata-integrity compares the digest produced from that collection.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The parser collection feeds computeSourceFingerprintForFolder and the strict validator consumes that digest; independent packet contracts recognize acceptance-criteria.md.
findingDetails.recommendation: Include acceptance-criteria.md in the fingerprint set and bump the generation, or explicitly document and test its exclusion.
findingDetails.claim: The current-generation source fingerprint does not detect edits to acceptance-criteria.md.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: A separate acceptance-criteria hash or validation path.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Acceptance criteria may be intentionally excluded, but no exclusion is documented.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: An explicit exclusion contract or independent acceptance-criteria digest is proven.

noveltyJustification: This is a new current-source cross-consumer boundary finding in the detached lineage; prior fanout stale-test and path-heuristic hypotheses were reread and are fixed, not copied.

findingDetails.title: Resume path confinement is lexical and follows in-tree symlinks to external packets
findingDetails.evidence: Explicit and phase-child resolution accept paths after lexical allowed-root checks; later resume reads use those paths, so an in-root symlink can redirect reads outside the workspace.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both explicit/fallback folder resolution and phase-child pointer resolution were reread; each returns or propagates a non-canonical path after only lexical root checks, and subsequent resume reads are rooted from it.
findingDetails.recommendation: Canonicalize candidates and redirected children, compare them with canonical allowed roots using a separator boundary, and retain canonical paths for subsequent reads; add external-target symlink fixtures.
findingDetails.claim: A symlink under an allowed specs root can redirect resume reads outside the workspace.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: A realpath-based check or later canonical-path recheck before reading resume documents.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The workspace may be fully trusted and symlinks may be intentionally allowed, but the implementation describes escape prevention and does not state such an exception.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If callers prove workspace roots cannot contain attacker-controlled symlinks and resume results never cross a trust boundary.

findingDetails.title: Graph metadata write guard accepts external paths merely containing a specs segment
findingDetails.evidence: isSpecsScopedPath accepts any absolute path containing /specs/; the writer canonicalizes a symlink target and then uses that lexical classifier as its final write authorization.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The classifier has no workspace/root parameter or filesystem-root comparison, while both graph write and refresh paths rely on it after realpath.
findingDetails.recommendation: Authorize writes against explicit canonical workspace specs roots, reject canonical targets outside those roots, and test arbitrary external /specs/ paths plus an in-root symlink.
findingDetails.claim: Graph metadata refresh/write can write outside supported workspace roots when an external path contains a specs segment.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: A universal caller-level canonical workspace-root check before the graph writer.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Current production callers may pass only trusted discovered paths, but the exported writer's stated boundary is not enforced for direct use or future callers.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If the exported API is wrapped so every call performs canonical-root authorization, with a test proving the wrapper is universal.

findingDetails.title: Unknown future fingerprint generations silently disable the integrity mismatch check
findingDetails.evidence: The validator returns for every source_fingerprint_docset other than the current marker, while the schema accepts any positive integer; an unknown future marker therefore suppresses mismatch reporting.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The early return is unconditional for non-current values and the schema has no known-generation set or upper bound; the parser persists the current marker at graph-metadata-parser.ts:1471-1474.
findingDetails.recommendation: Grandfather only explicitly known older generations; surface unknown/future generations as an integrity warning or error and add a mismatching-digest future-marker fixture.
findingDetails.claim: A future positive fingerprint-generation marker suppresses current-generation digest mismatch reporting.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: A documented supported-future-generation contract or independent check rejecting unknown markers.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The skip may intend forward compatibility, but this validator cannot distinguish a future generator from a forged or malformed marker.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If version negotiation explicitly makes unknown generations non-blocking and an independent check prevents stale data being treated as current.

findingDetails.title: Repair writes have a scan-to-write symlink race
findingDetails.evidence: Static discovery rejects symlink entries, but the non-dry-run loop later copies and writes the previously discovered pathname without inode/type revalidation or a no-follow boundary.
findingDetails.scopeProof: graphFiles filters with Dirent.isFile during discovery; the later write loop performs no canonical revalidation before copyFileSync/writeFileSync.
findingDetails.recommendation: Revalidate immediately before writing and use canonical temp-file plus rename or no-follow open semantics; document the maintenance command trust model.

noveltyJustification: Three new current-source security boundary findings cover symlinked resume reads, external graph writes, and unbounded generation skips; one advisory repair race is distinct. The prior acceptance-criteria omission was not duplicated.

findingDetails.title: The verification checklist claims closure while a required P1 item is explicitly deferred without approval
findingDetails.evidence: The local protocol requires P1 completion or user approval, CHK-FIX-006 remains unchecked, and the summary reports P1 0/0 and Verification Date: Not yet while acceptance-criteria.md says Closeable: Yes.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The protocol, unchecked item, summary, and closure rows were directly compared; no packet-local approval or exception is recorded.
findingDetails.recommendation: Complete the item, record the required approval, or amend the protocol and regenerate the summary/closure claim.
findingDetails.claim: The packet cannot truthfully claim a complete verification checklist while CHK-FIX-006 is unchecked because its protocol requires every P1 item to be complete or user-approved.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: A packet-local approval, ADR, or explicit protocol scope authorizing this P1 deferral.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The deferred note may be intended as an accepted exception, but no approval or exception rule is present and documented-only deferral is reserved for P2.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A recorded approval, a checked item with evidence, or an explicit protocol amendment governing this exception.

findingDetails.title: AC-007 does not provide evidence for the full rules/server/scripts scope named by REQ-005
findingDetails.evidence: REQ-005 names rules, server modules, and scripts, but AC-007 reports only rules, live templates, and spec-kit-docs.json; T006's concrete zero claim is limited to scripts/rules and the aggregate 35-file statement names no MCP/script results.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The normative requirement, criterion, task evidence, and implementation-summary scope were directly compared; no named server-module or non-rule-script result is retained.
findingDetails.recommendation: Attach the exact bounded search/output for every enumerated rules, MCP-module, and script surface, or narrow the requirement and criterion to the checked scope.
findingDetails.claim: AC-007 is marked Met without evidence covering all producer/consumer categories named by REQ-005.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: A named search artifact or command output covering every MCP server module and script in the declared inventory.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The aggregate 35-file statement may represent a complete search outside the packet, but it identifies neither the command nor the file/result set needed for independent acceptance.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A reproducible full-scope search record or a corrected criterion whose scope matches retained evidence.

findingDetails.title: Fingerprint-generation coverage is claimed in the task matrix but absent from the cited test surface
findingDetails.evidence: CHK-FIX-005 claims 16 rows cover id shape, source document, and fingerprint generation, but check-ac-coverage.sh exercises evidence parsing/source selection only and its bounded test search has no fingerprint-generation symbols; AC-003/004 retain manual baseline/edit claims without a named generation fixture or command.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The cited shell suite was read end-to-end; the exact fingerprint producer and validator are separate surfaces and are not invoked by that suite.
findingDetails.recommendation: Add or name a test covering stale-generation, current no-drift, and current drift cases against the producer/consumer pair and retain its command/output, or remove fingerprint generation from the 16-row claim.
findingDetails.claim: The packet's retained test evidence proves the fingerprint-generation axis and AC-003/AC-004 behavior.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: A separate named MCP/server test or committed fixture/output exercising generation mismatch and current drift.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The packet may rely on an ad hoc live sample outside the unit suite; without a command, fixture, or retained output it cannot independently verify the matrix claim.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A directly named executable test and retained result covering stale-generation compatibility and current-generation drift.
